fda-aha.title: FDA Alpha Hydroxy Acids
fda-aha.scope: 미국 FDA 소비자 안내. 한국 법규·제품별 안전성 판정 아님.
excerpts: The extent of exfoliation depends on the type and concentration of the AHA, its pH, and other ingredients in the product.
Use a sunscreen, wear protective clothing, and limit sun exposure while using this product and for a week afterwards.
The most common AHAs in cosmetic products are glycolic acid and lactic acid. Among others are citric acid, hydroxycaprylic acid, and hydroxycapric acid.

fda-bha.title: FDA Beta Hydroxy Acids
fda-bha.scope: 미국 FDA 소비자 안내. 한국 법규·제품별 안전성 판정 아님.
excerpts: If you use cosmetics with BHAs and experience skin irritation or prolonged stinging, stop using the product and consult your physician.
Avoid using BHA-containing products on infants and children.
Use sun protection if you use a BHA product.

fda-allergens.title: FDA Allergens in Cosmetics
fda-allergens.scope: 미국 FDA 소비자 안내. 한국 법규·제품별 안전성 판정 아님.
excerpts: Cosmetic products (such as soaps, lotions, makeup, fragrances, etc.) can provoke allergic reactions in some consumers.
An allergen can trigger the immune system to activate a defensive response that results in allergy symptoms.

d4.title: PubChem Octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane / HSDB
excerpts: Using OECD Guideline 310 (Ready Biodegradability - CO2 in Sealed Vessels, Headspace Test) and an activated sewage sludge inoculum, octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane, at 10 mg/L, reached only 3.7% of its theoretical CO2 evolution in 29 days(2).
underlying_references: (2) ECHA; Search for Chemicals. Octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane (CAS 556-67-2) Registered Substances Dossier. European Chemical Agency. Available from, as of Aug 17, 2015: https://echa.europa.eu/
